purpose: Exact additive native Keyring, capability, validator identity binding and frozen Config46 schema integration. Original production baseline hashes remain authoritative; historical verifier and constructor bytes are retained.

crypto/smartcont/config-code.fc.text:
;; Impure because it is: the checkpoint it reads back is published through a
;; global, and a caller that wants only that -- an entry point which does not
;; otherwise read the account -- would otherwise have its call elided for
;; having discarded every returned value.

;;
    ;; Asked here too, and that is the whole of the fail-closed rule rather
    ;; than an extra. A replacement contract is the strongest in-protocol
    ;; recovery there could be -- it can seed a checkpoint and drop every rule
    ;; above -- so leaving this one open would keep the recovery path that the
    ;; rest of this file no longer has, with the authority resting on a single
    ;; key. The absence of a checkpoint grants nothing, this action included.
    require_registry_checkpoint();

crypto/smartcont/elector-code.fc.text:
if (named_identity) {
    members~udict_set_builder(256, validator_pubkey, begin_cell()
      .store_tomis(msg_value)
      .store_uint(now(), 32)
      .store_uint(max_factor, 32)
      .store_uint(src_addr, 256)
      .store_uint(adnl_addr, 256)
      ;; in a reference, because the record plus another 256 bits no longer
      ;; fits a dictionary leaf beside its key
      .store_ref(begin_cell().store_uint(named_identity, 256).end_cell()));
  }
